017package org.apache.juneau.petstore.jetty;
018
019import java.util.*;
020
021import org.apache.juneau.commons.inject.*;
022import org.apache.juneau.commons.settings.*;
023import org.apache.juneau.microservice.*;
024import org.apache.juneau.microservice.examples.*;
025import org.apache.juneau.microservice.jetty.*;
026import org.apache.juneau.petstore.console.*;
027
028import jakarta.servlet.*;
029
030/**
031 * Petstore Jetty/Microservice deployment entry point.
032 *
033 * <p>
034 * Locates {@code juneau-petstore-jetty.cfg} (in the working directory or on the classpath), wires Jetty via
035 * {@link JettyConfiguration}, and mounts {@link RootResources} as the root servlet.
036 *
037 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
038 *    <li class='link'><a class="doclink" href="https://juneau.apache.org/docs/topics/JuneauPetstore">juneau-petstore</a>
039 * </ul>
040 */
041public class App {
042
043   /**
044    * Setting (system property, environment, or any registered source) listing the host names the admin resources
045    * answer to: comma-separated, no ports.  Unset or blank, only the loopback names {@link AdminBoundary#LOOPBACK_HOSTS}
046    * are answered.  Independent of {@value PetstoreApiBoundary#ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY}.
047    */
048   public static final String ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY = "petstore.admin.allowedHosts";
049
050   /**
051    * Entry point.
052    *
053    * @param args Command-line arguments forwarded to {@link Microservice}.
054    * @throws Exception If the microservice fails to start.
055    */
056   public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
057      // @formatter:off
058      Microservice
059         .create()
060         .args(args)
061         .configurations(JettyConfiguration.class, AppConfig.class)
062         .build()
063         .start()
064         .startConsole()
065         .join();
066      // @formatter:on
067   }
068
069   /**
070    * Application-specific configuration class contributing the top-level REST servlet and the console, API and admin
071    * boundary filters.
072    */
073   @Configuration
074   public static class AppConfig {
075
076      // Shared by both boundary beans: the console publishes tokens from the instance the API filter verifies them with.
077      private final PetstoreApiBoundary apiBoundary = new PetstoreApiBoundary();
078
079      /**
080       * Provides the top-level REST servlet, auto-mounted by {@code JettyServerComponent} at
081       * {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.Rest#path()}.
082       *
083       * @return The root servlet.
084       */
085      @Bean
086      public Servlet rootResources() {
087         return new RootResources();
088      }
089
090      /**
091       * Provides the console's CSRF boundary, covering {@code /console} only.
092       *
093       * <p>
094       * The {@code /petstore} API is covered by {@link #apiBoundary()} and the admin resources by
095       * {@link #adminBoundary()}; {@code /petstore-ui} is outside all three: see {@link PetstoreConsoleBoundary}.
096       * It runs ahead of routing and ahead of authentication, for the request, forward, async and error dispatches;
097       * the include dispatch is deliberately not mapped.  It is built over the same {@link PetstoreApiBoundary} that
098       * {@link #apiBoundary()} mounts, so the API token its pages carry is one the API filter accepts.
099       *
100       * @return The filter registration.
101       */
102      @Bean(name="consoleBoundary")
103      public ServletFilterRegistration consoleBoundary() {
104         return ServletFilterRegistration.create(new PetstoreConsoleBoundary(apiBoundary))
105            .urlPatterns(PetstoreConsoleBoundary.URL_PATTERN)
106            .dispatcherTypes(DispatcherType.REQUEST, DispatcherType.FORWARD, DispatcherType.ASYNC, DispatcherType.ERROR)
107            .order(ServletFilterRegistration.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE)
108            .build();
109      }
110
111      /**
112       * Provides the API's CSRF boundary, covering {@code /petstore/*}.
113       *
114       * <p>
115       * It runs only on the original request: an internal forward or error dispatch to the API is not a new
116       * attacker-controlled request.  The order keeps it just behind {@link #consoleBoundary()}; the two patterns never
117       * overlap.
118       *
119       * @return The filter registration.
120       */
121      @Bean(name="apiBoundary")
122      public ServletFilterRegistration apiBoundary() {
123         return ServletFilterRegistration.create(apiBoundary)
124            .urlPatterns(PetstoreApiBoundary.URL_PATTERN)
125            .dispatcherTypes(DispatcherType.REQUEST)
126            .order(ServletFilterRegistration.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 10)
127            .build();
128      }
129
130      /**
131       * Provides the admin resources' CSRF boundary, covering {@code /config}, {@code /logs} and {@code /shutdown}.
132       *
133       * <p>
134       * A filter of its own, answering to the host names in {@value App#ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY}, or to the
135       * loopback names only while that is unset.  The admin resources have no forms, so a browser write to them is
136       * refused, and command-line writes are admitted: see {@link AdminBoundary}.  The boundary does not authenticate:
137       * the admin resources must not be exposed on an untrusted network.
138       *
139       * @return The filter registration.
140       * @throws IllegalArgumentException If {@value App#ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY} holds an entry that is blank or
141       *    not a bare host name.
142       */
143      @Bean(name="adminBoundary")
144      public ServletFilterRegistration adminBoundary() {
145         return AdminBoundary.registration("", hosts(Settings.get().get(ADMIN_ALLOWED_HOSTS_PROPERTY).orElse(null)));
146      }
147
148      // The comma-separated entries, trimmed, blank ones kept so the boundary refuses them; none when unset.
149      private static String[] hosts(String setting) {
150         if (setting == null || setting.isBlank())
151            return new String[0];
152         return Arrays.stream(setting.split(",", -1)).map(String::trim).toArray(String[]::new);
153      }
154   }
155}
